Read link's output vocabulary

Source: R/lnk_vocabulary.R
lnk_vocabulary_read.Rd

The table of tokens that name what an output is: how its streams were cut (cut), which access rules decided where gradient barriers cut them (acc), how its gradient was measured (grad) and where its discharge came from (flow). lnk_vocabulary_resolve() matches a config against it, and every lnk_pipeline_run() records the four tokens in its <schema>.log row.

Usage

lnk_vocabulary_read()

Value

A data frame, one row per token, with columns token, axis (cut, acc, grad or flow), definition (prose), spec (the canonical string or digest lnk_vocabulary_resolve() matches), introduced (the link version that added it) and retired (the link version that retired it, NA while live).

Details

Tokens are lowercase, never renamed and never reused. A changed definition is a new token, and a retired token stays in the table so old names still decode. Consumers read this table (or inst/extdata/vocabulary.csv at a release tag) rather than copying it.

See also

Other vocabulary: lnk_vocabulary_resolve()

Examples

v <- lnk_vocabulary_read()
v[, c("token", "axis", "introduced")]
#>              token axis introduced
#> 1     cut-full-top  cut     0.70.0
#> 2 cut-full-ssf-all  cut     0.70.0
#> 3         acc-bcfp  acc     0.70.0
#> 4           acc-v1  acc     0.70.0
#> 5         grad-seg grad     0.70.0
#> 6          q-fwapg flow     0.70.0
#> 7       q-wet-fill flow     0.70.0
#> 8           acc-v2  acc     0.72.0
#> 9       acc-bcfp-2  acc     0.72.0
